question: does the synthetic-corpus egress result survive REAL text?
why_the_obvious_test_does_not_exist: the MVP path is retrieve -> text -> backbone -> answer, which carries NO typed labels. Running the typed head on MVP queries would require inventing labels. Refused.

method.prose: 992 unique sentences pooled from 19 committed design documents
method.typed_field: entity; label = the ONE entity the sentence mentions, by deterministic substring match
method.holdout: held-out sentences share an entity with training sentences but share no other tokens
method.control: SAME held-out rows, per-sample BLOCK permutation (D5-corrected)

what_this_does_establish.claim: written prose carries ~8.3x more codec content than my one-word templates
what_this_does_establish.correction: an earlier report cited '98.83% filler'. That number described a 3-word TEMPLATE, not written text. Real prose measures 98.58% unfilled, so the direction holds but the magnitude was a template artifact. The correction is recorded against my own earlier statement.

what_this_does_not_establish.claim: typed entity transfer on real prose
what_this_does_not_establish.reason: pre-registered 0.80 bar NOT met; n=12 held-out is far too small
what_this_does_not_establish.directional_note: 8/12 correct vs chance 3/12 is above chance (binomial p ~ 0.0028), so a signal is plausibly present. It is NOT a result at this n, and the control below chance does not license reading it.

defects_caught_before_the_run.D24: unit(Xte) on a 2-D matrix returns the FROBENIUS norm, so every row was divided by the same wrong scalar; accuracy would have been meaningless. Fixed with per-row normalisation.
defects_caught_before_the_run.D25: the control re-shuffled buckets and re-encoded, so control rows were DIFFERENT sentences. Fixed to permute the SAME held-out rows.
defects_caught_before_the_run.D26: rows_of() indexed [0] assuming encode_egress returns (bytes, ndarray) like encode(). It returns the ndarray directly, so [0] was the first row (8 floats). The shipped module's docstring was right; my probe was wrong.
defects_caught_before_the_run.D27: the D26 patch fixed the function but left [0] at all three call sites (partial fix).
defects_caught_before_the_run.D28: one document yielded 74 sentences and no entity reached 6 unambiguous ones; the gate correctly returned TABLE_REPORTED. Pooling committed documents gave 992 sentences.

honest_limits: K=4 and n=12 held-out: too small for a claim in either direction
n=12 held-out: 8/12 correct is 4 above chance, but the pre-registered bar is 0.80
the label rule matches substrings, so a sentence containing an entity name in a quoted context could be mislabelled; unambiguous single-entity sentences were required
